case.headline: A filed report explains this 13 ppb episode.

reasoning.claim: The monitor recorded 13 ppb at its peak on Apr 13, 2023, 3:00 PM, against a background near 0.2 ppb, over 1 hours.
Through the episode the wind came from the south-east, modelled.
The closest filed report is incident 398929 from Blanchard Refining Galveston Bay Refinery, listing 3716.55 pounds, with 100% of the episode's hours inside its window.

innocent_explanations: A release below the reportable quantity would leave no filed report at all.
Permitted, routine emissions can build up when the air is still and the plume stays low.
what_would_settle_it: Sub-hourly data from the monitor for this window, which would show whether the rise was a sharp plume or a slow build.
Any complaint or investigation records the agency holds for this date.
case.request_draft:
To: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, Public Information Coordinator
Subject: Public information request, air monitoring and incident records, Texas City

Dear Public Information Coordinator,

Under the Texas Public Information Act, I request copies of the following records.

1. All ambient air monitoring data, at the finest time resolution held, for monitor 48-167-0005 from Apr 13, 2023, 3:00 PM to Apr 13, 2023, 4:00 PM local time.
2. Any citizen complaints, investigation reports or field notes relating to air quality in Texas City for that period.
3. Any emission event, maintenance, startup or shutdown notifications received for facilities in Galveston County covering that period, including any submitted after the deadline.

This is a request for public records. It is not an allegation that any facility did anything improper.

If any portion is withheld, please cite the exemption claimed and release the remainder. If fees will exceed $50, please contact me first with an estimate.

Sincerely,
[your name]
[your address]
[your email and phone]
